$comment: LEGAL PROPOSITIONS — what a clause exists to implement, as distinct from the law it cites.
D4.5 established that 198 of 315 clauses declare no primary authority, and that citation
counts cannot stand in for one: Indian Contract Act 1872 s.73 is cited by 26 clauses across
13 categories as background ('damages for breach'), not because 26 clauses implement one
damages treatment. Without a declared proposition there is no way to tell a clause's own
rule from its supporting law — which is how a principal-employer liability allocation under
EPF s.8A came to live inside a clause about key personnel with nothing marking it separate.
A PROPOSITION IS NOT A STATUTE. The authority says where the rule comes from; the
proposition says what rule the clause implements. Several propositions can derive from one
section, and one proposition can rest on several. Collapsing the two would rebuild the
statute->clause shortcut this layer exists to replace.
THIS IS A SAMPLE, DELIBERATELY BIASED TOWARD FINDING REUSE. It covers variant-slot groups
(clauses the library already calls alternatives), a suspected overlapping pair, the known
composite clause, and a CONTROL SET of clauses that should share nothing. The control set is
load-bearing: a method that assigns the same proposition to everything would score high on
reuse while measuring nothing, so the falsification only means something if the controls stay
distinct.
Every record is unreviewed. An advocate must confirm that the statement is what the cited
authority actually establishes before any of this is relied on.

applicability says WHEN the rule applies, independently of which clause happens to implement it. That independence is the whole point: a clause may be selected on a narrower condition than a proposition it carries, and the proposition is then lost whenever the clause is not selected.

propositions.statement: A recipient of information identified as confidential is bound not to disclose or use it outside the permitted purpose.

authority.note: A confidentiality restraint is not a restraint of trade where it protects information rather than the right to compete.

propositions.statement: Where the information includes trade secrets, the obligation is of a higher order and does not lapse with time.

authority.note: Indian law protects trade secrets through contract; there is no separate trade secrets statute.

propositions.applicability_note: Applicable only where the information includes trade secrets.

propositions.statement: A security deposit is limited in amount and must be returned on vacancy subject only to stated deductions.

authority.note: Caps the deposit and fixes the period for its refund.
A deduction that is a penalty rather than compensation for actual loss is not recoverable in full.

propositions.statement: Rent is payable in a stated amount at a stated interval, with the tax treatment of the payment identified.

authority.note: Rent is an essential term of a lease.
Deduction of tax at source on rent.

propositions.statement: Where the parties intended performance by particular individuals, the promisor may not substitute freely; absent that intention the statutory default permits substitution by a competent person.

authority.note: Sets the default: the promisor or his representatives MAY employ a competent person, unless the nature of the case shows personal performance was intended. A key-person clause displaces the default; it does not create a restriction from nothing.

propositions.applicability_note: Applicable only where the parties intended performance by particular individuals. Absent that intention ICA s.40's default permits substitution, and the clause has nothing to displace.

propositions.statement: Personnel deployed under a services engagement remain the service provider's own workers, and responsibility for their wages and statutory contributions rests with it rather than with the client.

authority.note: Responsibility for payment of wages rests with the employer.

authority.act: Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
authority.note: Recovery from a principal employer in respect of contract labour — the exposure this allocation is drafted to keep with the service provider.

propositions.applicability_note: Always applicable to a services engagement: the client's exposure as principal employer does not depend on whether particular individuals matter, nor on whether service levels were agreed.

propositions.statement: The borrower's obligation to repay is fixed as to amount and timing.

authority.note: The parties must perform their promises; a repayment promise must be certain enough to perform.

propositions.statement: The parties choose the law governing the agreement and the courts that will hear disputes under it.

authority.note: Where more than one court has jurisdiction, the parties may agree to confine disputes to one of them.

propositions.statement: Communications under the agreement take effect only if given by a stated method, and are deemed received at a stated time.

authority.note: Time and place of despatch and receipt of an electronic record.

propositions.statement: A lease for a term exceeding one year takes effect only if made by a registered instrument; an unregistered one is inadmissible to prove the lease.

authority.note: A lease of immovable property from year to year, or for a term exceeding one year, is compulsorily registrable.
An unregistered instrument that the Act requires to be registered cannot be received as evidence of the transaction.
Such a lease can be made only by a registered instrument.

propositions.applicability_note: Registration Act s.17(1)(d) bites on a lease from year to year or for a term exceeding one year. `is_registrable` is derived from the actual term and is already correct — true for a 24-month rental, false for a 3-month lease. Two earlier authorings of this field were wrong and each was caught: `always: true` made a 3-month lease report the proposition satisfied by a clause whose rendered text says registration is NOT compulsory, and a guessed control name made the annotation inert. The fact existed the whole time.
propositions.outside_the_document: Registration is an act performed on the instrument before the Sub-Registrar after execution. A clause can require it, allocate its cost and record the consequence of failing to do it. Nothing a document says can accomplish it, so the highest finding available is PROVIDED_FOR.

propositions.statement: Source code is placed with an escrow agent and released to the customer on defined events such as the developer's insolvency or prolonged maintenance default.

authority.note: A moratorium can suspend enforcement against the corporate debtor, which is what an escrow release event triggered by insolvency has to survive.

propositions.applicability_note: Applicable only where the parties elected escrow.
propositions._polarity_note: Authored to test whether the model can tell an asserted proposition from a negated one. TECH_SOURCE_CODE_001 states the obligation in one world and states its absence in the other, under the same clause id.

propositions.statement: The parties intend their arrangement to create legal relations and to be enforceable between them.

authority.note: An agreement is a contract when made with free consent, for consideration, with a lawful object, and by parties competent to contract — intention to create legal relations is what distinguishes an enforceable bargain from a record of understanding.

propositions.applicability_note: Applicable where the parties intend a binding instrument. Where they do not, the proposition is not applicable and the document correctly says so in its own words.
propositions._polarity_note: The CONTROL for the escrow case. The same driver selects between two clause ids asserting opposite positions, so `implements` on a clause id is world-correct without any new mechanism.
